questions_visited.why_selected: A direct two-mark Newton-law statement establishes required exact wording.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: State mass-product and inverse-square proportionalities for point masses.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Translate the verbal law into F proportional to m1m2 divided by r squared.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Omitting the square on separation or failing to state the point-mass condition.

questions_visited.why_selected: Independent direct recall confirms the same recurring exam demand.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: State Newton's law accurately without a numerical prompt.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Identify direct proportionality to both masses and inverse-square separation.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Saying force is inversely proportional to r instead of r squared.
lesson_sections_informed: A fast route when only a factor changes

questions_visited.why_selected: Requires the equation and the name of G, complementing word-only law prompts.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Write Newton's equation and identify the universal gravitational constant.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Select F equals G times both masses divided by squared centre separation.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Using an unexplained G or putting the distance outside the squared denominator.
lesson_sections_informed: The calculation form of the law

questions_visited.why_selected: Tests the real-world boundary of the point-mass model.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Explain why measured force may differ from Newton-law calculation for real spheres.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Check the point-mass, uniformity, isolation and other-force assumptions.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Treating the model as exact for finite, non-uniform or non-isolated objects.

questions_visited.reasoning_route: Replace a uniform sphere with a central point mass, then use centre distance in the later potential relationship.
